title: Daemon clone rebuild (Modules A–E, #4041/#4044)
summary: A resident daemon (review-daemon, reconcile-fix-dispatch-daemon) runs from its own dedicated clone. Every tick, before doing its real dispatch work, it rebuilds that clone FRESH from origin/main plus its registered overlay list, in the object database, under the clone's own reader/writer lock, gated by a live smoke that runs while still holding the write lock. Pass -> reset --hard onto the new tree, then a restart-throttle decides whether to actually restart the process (launchd relaunches it) or keep ticking on the already-updated-on-disk tree. Fail -> roll back to the pre-move HEAD and the SAME tick continues on the old, still-in-memory code. A clone the rebuild cannot move stays behind main; a dispatch chokepoint elsewhere (main-staleness.mjs#assertMainNotStale) then refuses every dispatch from it as STALE. An operator (or a one-shot CLI) can also register an overlay ref by hand at any time, independent of the tick loop.

provides.note: launchd sets WorkingDirectory=/Users/nicolasgilbert/workspace/wev-review-daemon; the fix-dispatch-daemon plist carries the identical WorkingDirectory (both daemons share ONE clone).

provides.name: <daemon-state-dir>
provides.note: WE_DAEMON_STATE_DIR override, else ~/.claude/daemon-self-sync-state — confirmed present on this host with real <cloneKey>.rebuild.json/.alerts.jsonl files for two clone keys.

provides.name: WE_DAEMON_MANAGED_CLONE
provides.note: Set to '1' on process.env at withSelfSync construction, before the first tick — every child this daemon spawns inherits it.

provides.name: pool root = <workspace>/.lanes

states.label: Daemon tick begins (withSelfSync wrapper)
states.owner: review-daemon | reconcile-fix-dispatch-daemon (whichever process ticks; identical wiring)
states.notes: Tick cadence is 120s (DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS) for both daemons; runDaemonLoop's own try/catch (review-daemon.mjs:129-134) means ANY exception anywhere in this whole flow that reaches back up to tickOnce is caught, logged via onTickError (stderr only, into the plist's StandardErrorPath log file — no notify/label/card), and the loop just sleeps to the next tick. That is the ultimate 'escalation' for every otherwise-unhandled failure below.

states.label: rebuildClone takes the clone's write lock

wait.for: the writer key (refused outright if a live foreign writer holds it) + every already-live reader on this clone to drain or lapse

states.notes: #4044: this wait used to be silently up to daemon-clone-lock.mjs's own 600s default (WE_DAEMON_CLONE_LOCK_WAIT_MS) with NO log line at all; rebuildClone now supplies its own shorter 60s bound plus an onBlocked callback that logs once ('waiting up to Ns for live reader(s) ... #4044') before it starts waiting (daemon-rebuild.mjs:696-703). A concurrent-mover (another writer already holds the key) is refused immediately, no wait at all (daemon-clone-lock.mjs:250-253).

states.label: Rebuild skipped this tick — tick runs on the current (unmoved) tree
states.notes: Unlike every other 'not moved' outcome below, this one does NOT wait for the next 120s tick: the SAME tick immediately falls through to acquiring the read lock and running the real dispatch body on whatever tree is currently on disk. That dispatch body is a different flow's territory (review dispatch / fix dispatch), handed off below.

states.label: Step 0-1: crash recovery + local-tree safety check

retries.what: a stale .git/index.lock is auto-recovered once it is older than a threshold

states.notes: index-lock recovery threshold defaults to 120000ms (WE_DAEMON_INDEX_LOCK_STALE_MS); interrupted-rebuild recovery threshold defaults to 30 min (WE_DAEMON_REBUILD_STALE_MS). A dirty tree caused ONLY by a known tracked daemon-state file (scripts/conveyor/run-scorecards.json) is migrated out of the tree automatically (migrateDaemonStateFiles, lines 828-833) before the safety check is re-run; any other dirt still refuses.

states.label: Clone stuck — needs a hand git reset --hard / manual file fix
states.ownerCite: scripts/lib/daemon-rebuild.mjs:14-20 (file header: 'git clean is NEVER called... wiping it is not this module's business'); :773-815 (rebuild-interrupted-unrecoverable, quarantine)
states.notes: FOLDS FOUR distinct no-automatic-recovery conditions the code itself treats identically (every tick just re-hits the same check and re-refuses): (a) rebuild-interrupted-unrecoverable — a crashed rebuild whose on-disk HEAD matches neither its recorded target nor a clean prevHead (daemon-rebuild.mjs:792-796); (b) quarantine — a failed post-smoke rollback or reset itself failed (:799-815, :944, :986, :1024-1028); (c) a persistently unsafe tree (dirty/local-commits/merge-in-progress/status-failed) that migrateDaemonStateFiles could not clear (:834-837); (d) overlay-state-corrupt, a hand-edited or half-written overlay list file (:854-857, scripts/lib/daemon-overlays.mjs:18-24). NONE of these four has an owner or a timeout: nothing here ever alerts an operator beyond the alerts.jsonl line + a stderr log line (daemon-rebuild.mjs's own `alert()`, lines 734-742) — this IS the silent-failure gap. The module's own docs say a human `git reset --hard`/file-fix is required; nothing pages anyone to do it.

states.label: Step 2-4: fetch origin/main + overlays, planRebuild, apply list edits, short-circuit if nothing to do

retries.what: a batched fetch failure retries main alone, then each overlay ref individually

states.notes: planRebuild (lines 173-294) walks the overlay list in order, auto-removing anything main/PR state already made moot and conflict-dropping anything that doesn't merge cleanly THIS pass (never destructively, decisions are only applied back to the list afterward). still-rejected (line 904-912) gets a growing backoff ONLY when every prior failure was external-only (gh/network); a genuine code-shaped rejection has NO backoff/cap at all — it stays rejected until the inputsKey itself changes (main or the overlay moves). See the `smoke-code-reject-rollback` state for the same uncapped-retry gap stated precisely.

states.label: A pinned overlay conflicts with main (or is gone) — whole rebuild refused
states.notes: GAP distinct from clone-held-stale: a pinned-overlay refusal returns `finish({moved:false, reason: plan.reason, ...})` WITHOUT a `plan` field (daemon-rebuild.mjs:870-874), so it never satisfies finish()'s own condition for the loud 'clone-held-stale' alert (`result.plan?.ok && !result.plan.upToDate`, lines 743-753) that every OTHER stuck-and-behind outcome gets. The only signal is the original alert(plan.reason, plan.detail) call carrying PINNED_OVERLAY_MESSAGE/PINNED_OVERLAY_GONE_MESSAGE (lines 136-138, 872-874) — a human must already know to grep the alerts log for THIS specific reason string rather than the more discoverable clone-held-stale one. This is arguably the MOST likely to need a human (rebase the pinned branch, or unpin/re-register it) yet gets the WEAKEST signal of the stuck states.

states.label: Step 5: git reset --hard onto the planned build (the ONLY tree-moving call in this module)
states.notes: smokeOnly path (a prior rebuild crashed after its own reset landed but before its smoke ran) skips this reset entirely — the tree is already at the target — and goes straight to live smoke, rolling back to the ORIGINAL pre-interrupt head (not just prevHead) on a later failure (lines 890, 930).

states.label: Step 6: live smoke runs — STILL holding the clone's write lock

retries.what: a 'transient' verdict (env/infra noise only — gh 401s, rate limits, a momentarily-exhausted lane pool) retries the WHOLE smoke

states.notes: THE CENTRAL FINDING #2731 exists to fix, confirmed on MAIN as-is: this whole smoke (lane-pool acquire/release with up to a 180s internal wait, 3x gh calls, a reconcile-pass dry-run per constellation repo, a dispatch-dry-run) runs with `cwd: root` == the SAME clone every other daemon on this host reads from, INSIDE the SAME withWriteLock hold that rebuildClone took to do its `reset --hard` (daemon-rebuild.mjs:706-708,935-963) — every daemon sharing this clone is refused 'writer-active' at its own acquireRead for the smoke's ENTIRE duration (measured live at up to 209s, daemon-rebuild.mjs:528-536's own comment). A slow smoke (>=60000ms, SLOW_SMOKE_ALERT_MS) is alerted (daemon-rebuild.mjs:656-657,966-971) but the write lock is never released early. THE CANDIDATE ENV ON MAIN, AS-IS: cwd is literally `root` (no isolation — the reset in the prior state already moved `root` onto the candidate sha, so there is no separate 'candidate' tree at all on main today) and `env` is whatever was passed into rebuildClone (defaults to `process.env` — the SAME ticking daemon's launchd-provided env when a tick calls it, or an operator's own shell env when scripts/lib/daemon-load-overlay.mjs is run by hand). Because cwd IS root, path-derived env like the lane-pool root (scripts/lib/lane-pool-paths.mjs:40-44,65-68 `workspaceFor(checkoutRoot)`, since LANE_POOL_ROOT itself is never explicitly set anywhere here) resolves to the SAME pool root the live (post-adopt) daemon uses, purely because they share the same cwd. See this report's prose for why the OPEN #2731 branch's candidate-worktree redesign reintroduces exactly this class of mismatch.

states.label: Smoke verdict pass — build adopted
states.notes: state.adopted + state.rejected=null written under the state-root before the write lock is released (writeRebuildState, line 978).

states.label: decideRestart — did the move touch a file this daemon actually imports, and has it run long enough?
states.notes: minIntervalMs defaults to 10 min (DEFAULT_RESTART_MIN_INTERVAL_MS, WE_DAEMON_RESTART_MIN_INTERVAL_MS). Deliberately NOT modeled as a retries cap: this is a THROTTLE, not a failure retry — it always eventually restarts once uptime clears the window (or never, if genuinely no imported file changed — 'no-imported-change' is a correct, permanent no-restart, not a stuck retry).

states.label: Daemon releases its lease and exits 0 — launchd relaunches it onto the new code
states.notes: This is a genuine process exit — the NEXT process instance re-enters this same flow at tick-start from scratch, with a fresh boot-time HEAD snapshot (daemon-self-sync.mjs:481-482).

states.label: Smoke verdict 'code' — genuine failure, rolled back and cached as rejected
states.notes: UNCAPPED, confirmed: state.rejected is written with no retryAt UNLESS every failed check is external-only (isExternalOnlyFailure, line 998); in that one sub-case a backoff is added (base 5min, doubling, capped at 60min via WE_DAEMON_REJECT_RETRY_MAX_MS, lines 660-664). A genuine code-shaped failure has NO backoff and NO cap at all — it stays rejected forever until the inputsKey changes (main moves, or the overlay list changes), by design (the file header calls this correct: 'the SAME broken build is never re-smoked every tick'), but nothing ever tells an operator it is sitting there rejected beyond the alerts log + the clone-held-stale line below.

states.label: Smoke verdict 'transient' even after retries — rolled back, NOT cached (env noise, not code)
states.notes: Deliberately never poisons the reject-cache (file header rationale) — every subsequent tick retries the full smoke again from scratch, so this self-heals once the environment recovers, at the cost of repeating the whole (potentially 60s+) smoke, under the write lock, every 120s tick until it does.

states.label: ALERT: rebuild is holding this clone off origin/main

escalation.how: alerts.jsonl line (kind:'clone-held-stale') + a stderr log line naming the reason and, if the clone was previously rejected under the same inputsKey, the recorded retryAt — no notify/label/card is filed automatically

states.notes: Fires whenever a tick ends with plan.ok===true, the plan is NOT up-to-date, and the tree was not moved/adopted (still-rejected, untracked-collision, reset-failed-but-rolled-back, smoke-rejected, smoke-transient). Notably does NOT fire for held-pinned-refusal (see that state's own notes) or for the stuck-needs-hand-fix conditions (plan never even reaches this check there).

states.label: A review/fix dispatch on this clone refuses — STALE code from this checkout
states.owner: none (assertMainNotStale only refuses; nothing un-sticks the clone from here)

escalation.how: the thrown error text (STALE_MAIN_REFUSAL_MARKER = 'STALE code from this checkout') tells the operator this is a DAEMON-MANAGED clone and points at '~/.claude/daemon-self-sync-state/<cloneKey>.alerts.jsonl' for the clone-held-stale reason — but this is a thrown exception inside ONE per-repo dispatch call, caught by the SAME generic per-repo try/catch every other tick failure uses (skills-src/conveyor/review-daemon.mjs:195-238's per-repo isolation), so it reads in the log as an ordinary 'repo tick failed unexpectedly' line unless a human already knows to grep for the marker text

states.notes: A managed clone NEVER auto-fast-forwards here by design (main-staleness.mjs:189-198) — only this flow's own gated rebuild may move it. A commit range that touches ONLY non-code files (e.g. backlog/*.md) is explicitly NOT stale for dispatch (#4044 guard, lines 200-211) — this state is reached only when the behind range includes at least one real code file, or the diff itself could not be read (fails closed to 'stale').

states.label: Operator registers/removes an overlay ref out-of-band (daemon-overlay.mjs / daemon-load-overlay.mjs)
states.owner: operator (or an automated caller running the same CLI)

wait.for: the overlay list's own mkdir mutex (daemon-overlays.mjs's withListLock), THEN (unless --no-lock) the clone's write lock
wait.timeout: list mutex: 20000ms fixed (LIST_LOCK_WAIT_MS); write lock: 600000ms default (WE_DAEMON_CLONE_LOCK_WAIT_MS) since scripts/daemon-overlay.mjs:84 calls withWriteLock with NO waitMs override at all, unlike rebuildClone's own 60s bound

states.notes: GAP: this CLI's write-lock wait is 10x longer than rebuildClone's own tick-start wait (600s vs 60s) with no onBlocked logging at all (scripts/daemon-overlay.mjs:84 passes `{}`), so an operator running this by hand while a slow live-smoke is in progress can sit silently for up to 10 minutes before seeing 'write lock refused'. `daemon-load-overlay.mjs` additionally calls rebuildClone() right after registering (its OWN write-lock acquire, the 60s-bounded one) — so a real early-load goes through BOTH lock waits in sequence. Either wait's timeout lands on cli-overlay-op-failed below — a list-mutex timeout THROWS (uncaught inside addOverlay/removeOverlay, caught only by the CLI's top-level `.catch`); a write-lock timeout returns `{ok:false, reason}` and the CLI prints 'write lock refused' — both end in the same exit-1-and-stop outcome, neither retries automatically.

states.label: The overlay CLI exits non-zero (lock wait exhausted) — no automatic retry
states.notes: The operator (or whatever automated caller ran this CLI) sees a non-zero exit and a one-line stderr message; nothing here schedules a follow-up attempt.

transitions.on: withSelfSync's wrapped tickOnce calls rebuild()
out-of-band: an operator (or automated caller) runs daemon-overlay.mjs add/remove or daemon-load-overlay.mjs at any time, independent of the tick loop
write lock acquired
waitMs elapsed with a live reader still holding a read slot ('tick-in-progress')
falls through to acquireRead + the ordinary dispatch tick body (review-daemon uses @review; fix-dispatch-daemon uses @fix identically)
daemon-overlay.mjs add/remove only mutates the list — no immediate rebuild; the NEXT regular tick's own acquire-write-lock picks the change up
daemon-load-overlay.mjs (--ref) registers the overlay AND calls rebuildClone() immediately, the same gated path a tick uses
unrecoverable interrupted rebuild, quarantine, or an unsafe tree migrateDaemonStateFiles could not clear
on main, tree verified safe, prevHead resolved
overlay-state-corrupt and not a main-only rebuild
planRebuild refuses: a pinned overlay conflicts with main this pass, or its ref/PR is gone without main having it
plan.upToDate — HEAD already equals the planned build, nothing to move
still-rejected: same inputsKey already rejected and its retry backoff (if any) has not elapsed
untracked-collision: a kept untracked file collides with real content in the target tree
plan.ok, not up-to-date, not (still-)rejected, no untracked collision
reset --hard failed AND the rollback to prevHead also failed
reset --hard failed but the rollback to prevHead succeeded — tree unchanged, still behind
reset landed (or smokeOnly: HEAD already at the planned build)
verdict === 'pass'
verdict === 'code' (a genuinely non-transient check failure)
verdict === 'transient' even after the retry cap
the post-smoke rollback itself failed, or the whole rebuild threw and ITS rollback also failed
state.adopted written
no imported file changed, or the min-restart-interval has not elapsed yet — keep ticking on the already-updated-on-disk tree
an imported file changed and the min-interval has elapsed
tick continues on the rolled-back (old) code
plan.ok and not up-to-date and not moved
tick continues on the rolled-back (old) code
plan.ok and not up-to-date and not moved
next scheduled tick (120s later) tries the rebuild again
a review/fix dispatch on this managed clone calls assertMainNotStale and it is still behind in code files
same real-world consequence while stuck: dispatch on this clone also refuses as stale
same real-world consequence — reached WITHOUT ever passing through the clone-held-stale alert (see held-pinned-refusal's own notes)
the list mutex (20s) or the write lock (600s default) times out

steps.does: for each planRebuild decision (remove/drop), removeOverlay() + appendOverlayEvent() against the per-clone overlay list file
steps.notes: THE FINDING: removeOverlay/appendOverlayEvent go through daemon-overlays.mjs's own withListLock mutex (20s bound, THROWS on timeout — daemon-overlays.mjs:139-169). This call site sits BEFORE doRebuild's own try/catch (which only starts at daemon-rebuild.mjs:935), so a thrown timeout here is NOT caught locally. It propagates out of withWriteLock (which still releases the write lock via its own finally, daemon-clone-lock.mjs:350-357) and out of `rebuild()` itself (daemon-self-sync.mjs:540, no try/catch there either) all the way up to runDaemonLoop's generic per-tick try/catch (skills-src/conveyor/review-daemon.mjs:129-134) — logged as an indistinguishable 'tick failed (non-fatal)' line, with the ENTIRE tick's real dispatch work skipped for that cycle, not just the rebuild. onFailure is genuinely null: no state in this flow specifically routes this failure anywhere.

steps.actor: runLiveSmokeWithRetry -> runLiveSmoke (daemon-live-smoke.mjs), invoked by doRebuild while still holding lock:daemon-clone-writer
steps.does: spawn each SMOKE_CHECKS row (lane-pool list/acquire/release, gh api, gh pr list, reconcile-pass --dry-run per constellation repo, a dispatch-dry-run child, and a final git-status-clean check), cwd: root, env: whatever was passed into rebuildClone

assumes.name: <daemon-clone>
assumes.note: root was already reset --hard onto the candidate sha by the previous step, so cwd here IS the real clone, not an isolated copy.

assumes.name: pool root = <workspace>/.lanes
assumes.note: the smoke acquires + releases a real lane with cwd = the root it smokes

provides.name: smoke lane acquired+released
provides.note: a real lane-pool.mjs acquire+release proving the pool machinery works, not just that it parses; leaks a lease (never auto-cleaned) if the release call itself fails (daemon-live-smoke.mjs:205-209).

steps.notes: Because cwd is literally the same root the live daemon is running from (no candidate worktree on main today), path-derived config like the lane pool root (LANE_POOL_ROOT unset anywhere in this whole flow; scripts/lib/lane-pool-paths.mjs:40-44,65-68 derives it from cwd) resolves to the SAME value the live post-adopt daemon will use, purely by cwd coincidence. See this task's report for why an off-lock redesign that smokes a SEPARATE worktree path must pin this explicitly or it silently mismatches.

steps.actor: addOverlay/removeOverlay (daemon-overlays.mjs), called from daemon-overlay.mjs or daemon-load-overlay.mjs
steps.does: withListLock: mkdir a `.lock` dir beside the overlay state file; poll/retry until acquired or LIST_LOCK_WAIT_MS elapses
steps.notes: A stuck mutex (another process's mkdir never removed, e.g. it died before its own finally) is reclaimed only once it is older than LIST_LOCK_STALE_MS (30000ms); until then this THROWS after 20000ms with no retry of its own — caught only by the CLI's own top-level .catch (cli-overlay-op-failed).

steps.does: withWriteLock(root, () => fn(), {}) — NO waitMs override, so acquireWrite's own 600000ms default applies

assumes.name: <daemon-clone>
assumes.note: resolved from the operator's own --clone= flag, not from a launchd-provided cwd.

steps.notes: A refusal (concurrent-mover, or a 10-minute timeout) prints 'write lock refused (<reason>)' and exits 1 — no retry, no escalation beyond the CLI's own exit code. Ten minutes is a LONG silent wait for an interactive operator compared to rebuildClone's own 60s bound for the same lock.
